heroHeadline: Treaty of Jeddah Signed — SAF and RSF Commit to Civilian Protection; Dilling Siege Broken Third Time, Famine-Stricken Kadugli Receives First Convoy Since January
heroSubtitle: On Day 1132, SAF and RSF signed the Treaty of Jeddah on May 20, brokered by Saudi Arabia and the United States, committing both parties to civilian safe passage, protection of relief workers, and prohibition on using civilians as human shields — the first formal humanitarian framework signed by both warring parties. The agreement arrived as SAF broke the Dilling siege for a third time in 2026, capturing Al-Takma in South Kordofan and reopening the Dilling–Kadugli road; the first supply convoy in four months reached famine-confirmed Kadugli (IPC Phase 5), collapsing sugar prices from SDG 40,000 to SDG 13,000/kg as civilians celebrated. Sudan's Security and Defence Council formally commended SAF gains across South Kordofan, Blue Nile, and Darfur. UN Human Rights Chief Türk's high-alert statement from May 11 — documenting 880+ civilian drone deaths in January–April 2026 (over 80% of all conflict deaths) — frames the week's events: the Treaty of Jeddah exists in acute tension with the reality of both sides continuing intensive drone campaigns. Sudan also began Ebola screening for arrivals from Uganda at Port Sudan airport. Total displacement stands at 14 million+ with 19.5 million facing acute food insecurity and a lean-season peak of 28.9 million projected for June–August 2026.
